steps.title: The inverse normal does the opposite job
steps.body:
In the last lesson you used Normal Cdf. You gave it a value, such as \(160\), and it told you the area to the left of that value: \(\mathrm{P}(X<160)=0.106\). The area is a probability.

Step 1 was the other way round. You were given the area (\(90\%\) of students are shorter than \(h\), so the area to the left of \(h\) is \(0.9\)) and asked for the value \(h\). The function for that is Inverse Normal: you give it the area, it gives you the value on the axis.

Two rules that make or break every inverse-normal question:
•  The area you type is always the area to the LEFT of the value you want. “\(90\%\) shorter than \(h\)” is a left area already: type \(0.9\).
•  If the question gives a percentage ABOVE, change it to below first. “The tallest \(7\%\) are above \(k\)” means \(93\%\) are below \(k\): type \(0.93\).
steps.code:
Normal Cdf:      you give a value \(160\)  \(\longrightarrow\)  it gives an area \(0.106\)
Inverse Normal:  you give an area \(0.9\)  \(\longrightarrow\)  it gives a value \(h=180.25\)

steps.body:

•  \(Q_3\) has \(75\%\) below it: area \(0.75\)

questions.stem: The heights of students at a school are normally distributed with mean \(170\) cm and standard deviation \(8\) cm.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the probability that a randomly chosen student is taller than \(180\) cm.
ms: \(\mathrm{P}(H>180)\), or a sketch with the right tail shaded
wrongs: Wrong tail: taller than \(180\) is the upper tail.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: \(20\%\) of the students are shorter than \(h\) cm. Find the value of \(h\).
parts.figCap: The area 0.2 is given; Inverse Normal returns the value h on the axis.
ms: \(\mathrm{P}(H<h)=0.2\), or a sketch with \(0.2\) shaded on the left
parts.note: The area typed into Inverse Normal is always the area to the left: \(0.2\) here, as given.
wrongs: \(176.7\) used area \(0.8\): that is the height \(80\%\) are shorter than. Here \(20\%\) are shorter.
That is \(z\); the question asks for the height \(h\).
That is the given probability; the answer is a height.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: The middle \(90\%\) of heights lie between \(a\) cm and \(b\) cm. Find \(a\) and \(b\).
parts.figCap: Middle 90% leaves 5% in each tail: a at area 0.05, b at area 0.95.
wrongs: That is the \(20\%\) value from (b); the middle \(90\%\) uses \(0.05\) and \(0.95\).
\(159.7\) used area \(0.1\): the tails share \(10\%\), so each is \(0.05\).

questions.stem: The scores in an examination are normally distributed with mean \(62\) and standard deviation \(11\).
